# hunk Hunk is an interactive terminal diff viewer for reviewing code changes, built on [OpenTUI](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui) and [Pierre diffs](https://www.npmjs.com/package/@pierre/diffs). **[hunk.dev](https://hunk.dev)** · [Documentation](https://hunk.dev/docs/) - multi-file review stream with sidebar navigation - inline AI and agent annotations beside the code - split, unified, and responsive auto layouts - watch mode for auto-reloading file and Git-backed reviews - keyboard, mouse, pager, and Git difftool support

Split view with sidebar and inline AI notes
Unified view and mouse-selectable menus
## Install On macOS and Linux, install the standalone binary: ```bash curl -fsSL https://hunk.dev/install.sh | sh ``` Windows users can install with npm or mise. Other installation methods are also available: ```bash npm i -g hunkdiff # macOS, Linux, or Windows; requires Node.js 22+ brew install hunk # macOS or Linux mise use -g hunk # macOS, Linux, or Windows ``` > [!NOTE] > If you previously installed hunk via `modem-dev/tap`, be sure to uninstall it first with `brew uninstall modem-dev/tap/hunk`. Windows requires mise 2026.8.6 or newer. Nix users can use the `default` package exported in `flake.nix`; see [the Nix guide](https://github.com/modem-dev/hunk/blob/main/nix/README.md) for details. Hunk also ships as a default tool in [Omarchy](https://omarchy.org), installed through mise. Requirements: - macOS (arm64, x64), Linux (arm64, x64; glibc), or Windows (x64); prebuilt binaries are not published for Windows on arm64 or musl-based Linux such as Alpine - On x86-64, a CPU with SSE4.2 (Intel Nehalem 2008+, AMD Bulldozer 2011+); arm64 has no CPU feature floor - Node.js 22+ for the npm install; the install script, Homebrew, mise, and Nix ship a standalone binary that does not require Node.js - Git recommended for most workflows ### Update Hunk For npm, Homebrew, and default install-script installs (Hunk 0.20+): ```bash hunk update # install the newest release hunk update --check # check without installing hunk update 0.20.0 # select an exact npm or default install-script release ``` On an older release, update once with the installer or package manager that installed Hunk, then use `hunk update` going forward. Custom `HUNK_INSTALL_DIR` installs must re-run the installer with the same directory; mise, Nix, and source installs use their owning tools instead. ## Quick start ```bash hunk # show help hunk --version # print the installed version ``` ### Working with Git Use familiar Git commands to open changes in Hunk: ```bash hunk diff # review current repo changes, including untracked files hunk diff --watch # auto-reload as the working tree changes hunk show # review the latest commit hunk show HEAD~1 # review an earlier commit hunk log # browse history on a terminal; print when redirected hunk log --static # force static output, paging when needed hunk status # view workspace status and sibling worktrees (Git) hunk status --static # print one read-only workspace snapshot hunk status --json # emit one versioned workspace snapshot ``` `hunk status` is read-only: it does not fetch or change the repository. See [workspace status](docs/status.md) for details. `hunk log` opens an interactive history browser in a terminal and prints text when piped or redirected. Use `--oneline` for compact output. In the browser, enable **Graph view** from the View menu to see commit branches, or press `v` to select a commit range. Quit a commit review to return to history. ### Working with GitHub Hunk bundles `hunk gh`, so pull requests, commits, and comparisons open directly without the GitHub CLI or a separate extension: ```bash hunk gh pr # infer the open PR for the current branch hunk gh pr 123 # infer the repository from origin hunk gh pr 'modem-dev/hunk#123' # quote this form for shells that treat # as a comment hunk gh commit a1b2c3d --repo modem-dev/hunk hunk gh compare main...feature --repo modem-dev/hunk ``` Public repositories work anonymously. Set `GH_TOKEN`, or `GITHUB_TOKEN` when it is absent, for private repositories and higher API limits. GitHub Enterprise is not currently supported. ### Working with Jujutsu and Sapling Hunk auto-detects Jujutsu and Sapling checkouts, so `hunk diff [revset]` and `hunk show [revset]` use native revsets inside jj or Sapling workspaces. `hunk log --vcs jj` also reads JJ history directly, including in a non-colocated workspace. To override VCS detection, set `vcs = "git"` or `vcs = "jj"` or `vcs = "sl"` in [config](#config). ### Viewing complete files and browsing directories ```bash hunk open # browse the current directory hunk open README.md # view a complete, syntax-highlighted document hunk open path/to/project # browse another directory without requiring a repository ``` Use arrows and Enter to navigate, Tab to switch focus, `i` to show hidden/Git-ignored entries, and `e` to edit the displayed file in `$EDITOR`. See [the open workflow](docs/open.md) for details and file limits. ### Working with raw files and patches ```bash hunk diff --files before.ts after.ts # compare two files directly hunk diff --files before.ts after.ts --watch # auto-reload when either file changes git diff --no-color | hunk patch - # review a patch from stdin ``` ### Working with agents 1. Install the review skill once: `npx skills add modem-dev/hunk -g --skill hunk-review`. 2. Open Hunk in another terminal with `hunk diff` or `hunk show`. 3. Ask your agent to use the hunk-review skill against the live Hunk session. 4. Press `a` in Hunk to show agent notes; they start hidden. If your agent has no skill system, ask it to run `hunk skill show` and follow the output. See [Review with an agent](https://hunk.dev/docs/agents/review-with-an-agent/) for live sessions, `--agent-context`, and experimental rich notes. ## Feature comparison | Capability | [hunk](https://github.com/modem-dev/hunk) | [lumen](https://github.com/jnsahaj/lumen) | [difftastic](https://github.com/Wilfred/difftastic) | [delta](https://github.com/dandavison/delta) | [diff-so-fancy](https://github.com/so-fancy/diff-so-fancy) | [diff](https://www.gnu.org/software/diffutils/) | | ------------------------------------ | ----------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------- | --------------------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------- | | Review-first interactive UI | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | Multi-file review stream + sidebar | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | Inline agent / AI annotations | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | Responsive auto split/unified layout | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | Mouse support inside the viewer | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | Runtime view toggles | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | Syntax highlighting | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | | Structural diffing | ❌ | ❌ | ✅ | ❌ | ❌ | ❌ | | Pager-compatible mode | ✅ | ❌ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ✅ | ## Advanced ### Config You can persist preferences to a config file: - `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/hunk/config.toml` (default `~/.config/hunk/config.toml`) - `.hunk/config.toml` in a repository Persistent state uses `$XDG_STATE_HOME/hunk/state.json` when the variable is absolute, or `~/.local/state/hunk/state.json` otherwise. Hunk preserves existing state by copying the old config-directory file on first use, keeping the original and falling back to it if migration fails. Global extension paths are unchanged. For example: ```toml theme = "github-dark-default" mode = "auto" # auto, split, unified auto_split_min_width = 160 # minimum available diff columns for split in auto mode line_numbers = true wrap_lines = false ``` See the [configuration guide](https://hunk.dev/docs/configure/configuration/) for command overrides and examples, the [full reference](https://hunk.dev/docs/reference/config/) for every option, or the [theme guide](https://hunk.dev/docs/configure/themes/) to customize colors. ### Keybindings Remap shortcuts with a `[keybindings]` table in your user config. readmeHtml:
hunk

Hunk is an interactive terminal diff viewer for reviewing code changes, built on OpenTUI and Pierre diffs.

hunk.dev · Documentation

  • multi-file review stream with sidebar navigation
  • inline AI and agent annotations beside the code
  • split, unified, and responsive auto layouts
  • watch mode for auto-reloading file and Git-backed reviews
  • keyboard, mouse, pager, and Git difftool support

Split view with sidebar and inline AI notes
Unified view and mouse-selectable menus

Install

On macOS and Linux, install the standalone binary:

curl -fsSL https://hunk.dev/install.sh | sh

Windows users can install with npm or mise. Other installation methods are also available:

npm i -g hunkdiff                    # macOS, Linux, or Windows; requires Node.js 22+
brew install hunk                    # macOS or Linux
mise use -g hunk                     # macOS, Linux, or Windows

Note

If you previously installed hunk via modem-dev/tap, be sure to uninstall it first with brew uninstall modem-dev/tap/hunk.

Windows requires mise 2026.8.6 or newer. Nix users can use the default package exported in flake.nix; see the Nix guide for details. Hunk also ships as a default tool in Omarchy, installed through mise.

Requirements:

  • macOS (arm64, x64), Linux (arm64, x64; glibc), or Windows (x64); prebuilt binaries are not published for Windows on arm64 or musl-based Linux such as Alpine
  • On x86-64, a CPU with SSE4.2 (Intel Nehalem 2008+, AMD Bulldozer 2011+); arm64 has no CPU feature floor
  • Node.js 22+ for the npm install; the install script, Homebrew, mise, and Nix ship a standalone binary that does not require Node.js
  • Git recommended for most workflows

Update Hunk

For npm, Homebrew, and default install-script installs (Hunk 0.20+):

hunk update          # install the newest release
hunk update --check  # check without installing
hunk update 0.20.0   # select an exact npm or default install-script release

On an older release, update once with the installer or package manager that installed Hunk, then use hunk update going forward. Custom HUNK_INSTALL_DIR installs must re-run the installer with the same directory; mise, Nix, and source installs use their owning tools instead.

Quick start

hunk           # show help
hunk --version # print the installed version

Working with Git

Use familiar Git commands to open changes in Hunk:

hunk diff                      # review current repo changes, including untracked files
hunk diff --watch              # auto-reload as the working tree changes
hunk show                      # review the latest commit
hunk show HEAD~1               # review an earlier commit
hunk log                       # browse history on a terminal; print when redirected
hunk log --static              # force static output, paging when needed
hunk status                    # view workspace status and sibling worktrees (Git)
hunk status --static           # print one read-only workspace snapshot
hunk status --json             # emit one versioned workspace snapshot

hunk status is read-only: it does not fetch or change the repository. See workspace status for details.

hunk log opens an interactive history browser in a terminal and prints text when piped or redirected. Use --oneline for compact output. In the browser, enable Graph view from the View menu to see commit branches, or press v to select a commit range. Quit a commit review to return to history.

Working with GitHub

Hunk bundles hunk gh, so pull requests, commits, and comparisons open directly without the GitHub CLI or a separate extension:

hunk gh pr                         # infer the open PR for the current branch
hunk gh pr 123                     # infer the repository from origin
hunk gh pr 'modem-dev/hunk#123'    # quote this form for shells that treat # as a comment
hunk gh commit a1b2c3d --repo modem-dev/hunk
hunk gh compare main...feature --repo modem-dev/hunk

Public repositories work anonymously. Set GH_TOKEN, or GITHUB_TOKEN when it is absent, for private repositories and higher API limits. GitHub Enterprise is not currently supported.

Working with Jujutsu and Sapling

Hunk auto-detects Jujutsu and Sapling checkouts, so hunk diff [revset] and hunk show [revset] use native revsets inside jj or Sapling workspaces. hunk log --vcs jj also reads JJ history directly, including in a non-colocated workspace. To override VCS detection, set vcs = "git" or vcs = "jj" or vcs = "sl" in config.

Viewing complete files and browsing directories

hunk open                 # browse the current directory
hunk open README.md       # view a complete, syntax-highlighted document
hunk open path/to/project # browse another directory without requiring a repository

Use arrows and Enter to navigate, Tab to switch focus, i to show hidden/Git-ignored entries, and e to edit the displayed file in $EDITOR. See the open workflow for details and file limits.

Working with raw files and patches

hunk diff --files before.ts after.ts        # compare two files directly
hunk diff --files before.ts after.ts --watch # auto-reload when either file changes
git diff --no-color | hunk patch -          # review a patch from stdin

Working with agents

  1. Install the review skill once: npx skills add modem-dev/hunk -g --skill hunk-review.
  2. Open Hunk in another terminal with hunk diff or hunk show.
  3. Ask your agent to use the hunk-review skill against the live Hunk session.
  4. Press a in Hunk to show agent notes; they start hidden.

If your agent has no skill system, ask it to run hunk skill show and follow the output.

See Review with an agent for live sessions, --agent-context, and experimental rich notes.

Feature comparison

Capability hunk lumen difftastic delta diff-so-fancy diff
Review-first interactive UI ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌
Multi-file review stream + sidebar ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌
Inline agent / AI annotations ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌
Responsive auto split/unified layout ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌
Mouse support inside the viewer ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌
Runtime view toggles ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌ ❌
Syntax highlighting ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅ ❌ ❌
Structural diffing ❌ ❌ ✅ ❌ ❌ ❌
Pager-compatible mode ✅ ❌ ✅ ✅ ✅ ✅

Advanced

Config

You can persist preferences to a config file:

  • $XDG_CONFIG_HOME/hunk/config.toml (default ~/.config/hunk/config.toml)
  • .hunk/config.toml in a repository

Persistent state uses $XDG_STATE_HOME/hunk/state.json when the variable is absolute, or ~/.local/state/hunk/state.json otherwise. Hunk preserves existing state by copying the old config-directory file on first use, keeping the original and falling back to it if migration fails. Global extension paths are unchanged.

For example:

theme = "github-dark-default"
mode = "auto"               # auto, split, unified
auto_split_min_width = 160  # minimum available diff columns for split in auto mode
line_numbers = true
wrap_lines = false

See the configuration guide for command overrides and examples, the full reference for every option, or the theme guide to customize colors.

Keybindings

Remap shortcuts with a [keybindings] table in your user config. See the keybinding guide for available commands, default keys, and examples.

Git integration

Set Hunk as your Git pager so git diff and git show open in Hunk automatically:

Note

Untracked files are auto-included only for Hunk's own hunk diff working-tree loader. If you open git diff through hunk pager, Git still decides the patch contents, so untracked files will not appear there.

git config --global core.pager "hunk pager"

Or in your Git config:

[core]
    pager = hunk pager

If you want to keep Git's default pager and add opt-in aliases instead:

git config --global alias.hdiff "-c core.pager=\"hunk pager\" diff"
git config --global alias.hshow "-c core.pager=\"hunk pager\" show"

Jujutsu pager integration

To use Hunk as jj's pager, run jj config edit --user and update:

[ui]
pager = ["hunk", "pager"]
diff-formatter = ":git"

Sapling pager integration

To use Hunk as Sapling's pager, run sl config -u and update:

[pager]
pager = hunk pager

Extensions (experimental)

The extension API is experimental and may change in breaking ways between minor releases while it stabilizes; breaking changes are called out in release notes.

Hunk loads plain TypeScript extensions from ~/.config/hunk/extensions/, from a repository's .hunk/extensions/ (after you explicitly trust that repository), and from --extension <path> for development. --no-extensions turns those off for one run; Hunk's own bundled backends (Git, Jujutsu, and Sapling) stay loaded.

Extensions can add commands, themes, VCS backends, custom sidebars, and more. For example, filter lockfiles out of a review:

// ~/.config/hunk/extensions/collapse-lockfiles.ts
import type { HunkExtensionAPI } from "hunkdiff/extension";

export default function (hunk: HunkExtensionAPI) {
  hunk.transformChangeset((changeset, ctx) => {
    const files = changeset.files.filter((file) => !file.path.endsWith(".lock"));
    ctx.notify(`Collapsed ${changeset.files.length - files.length} lockfiles`);
    return { ...changeset, files };
  });
}

Extensions shared as git repositories install straight from their host, and a hunk-extension GitHub topic marks community ones:

hunk extension install acme/hunk-word-diff@v1.2.0   # or git:host/path, a URL, a local path
hunk extension list                                 # then update [name] / remove <name>

Browse community extensions at github.com/topics/hunk-extension; publish yours by pushing the extension to a repository root and adding that topic.

See the extension guide for the API, configuration, and publishing instructions. Installable examples include review triage, review snapshot export, an optional rendered Markdown file view, and a Vim navigation mode built from public semantic commands.

OpenTUI component

Hunk also publishes HunkDiffView and lower-level primitives from hunkdiff/opentui for embedding the same diff renderer in your own OpenTUI app.

See the OpenTUI component guide for install, API, and runnable examples.

Examples

Ready-to-run demo diffs live in the examples directory.

Each example includes the exact command to run from the repository root.

Contributing

💬 Chat with users/contributors on the Modem Discord server

See CONTRIBUTING.md for development setup and contribution guidelines.

Sponsor

Sponsored by Modem.

License

MIT

releases.body:
## Hunk 0.24: beyond the diff

Hunk 0.24 brings complete-file and directory browsing, a live workspace compass, npm-installed extensions, and version-matched agent skills into your terminal review workspace. Worker highlighting makes startup interaction smoother, while a round of memory fixes keeps large reviews and long-running sessions leaner.

For npm- and curl-managed installs:

```sh
hunk update 0.24.0
npm install -g hunkdiff@0.24.0
```

Homebrew availability will be verified after publication; until then, Homebrew propagation is pending. The commands above select the exact release for npm- and curl-managed installations.

### Explore the source and find your next review

`hunk open` shows complete syntax-highlighted files and browses directories with lazy loading, live refresh, and keyboard or mouse navigation. Inspect the surrounding source without manufacturing a diff. The new read-only workspace status view brings together staging state, tracked and untracked changes, and sibling worktrees, with navigation into history and full diff reviews. Static and versioned JSON status output are available too. [#1148](https://github.com/modem-dev/hunk/pull/1148), [#1067](https://gith

## Hunk 0.24 beta: beyond the diff

This first 0.24 beta brings complete-file and directory browsing, a live workspace compass, and easier extension and agent setup into the same terminal workspace as your reviews. It also moves syntax highlighting into a worker by default and makes automatic diff layout respond to the space left by your side panes.

For npm- and curl-managed installs, select this beta explicitly:

```sh
hunk update 0.24.0-beta.0
npm install -g hunkdiff@0.24.0-beta.0
```

This is a prerelease. Stable installs continue to use 0.23.0; Homebrew does not distribute this beta.

aiSummary.oneLiner: A terminal-based, review-first diff viewer optimized for agent-authored changesets with interactive AI annotations.
aiSummary.whatItDoes: Hunk provides an interactive terminal UI specifically built for reviewing codebase changes, natively integrating with version control systems like Git, Jujutsu, and Sapling. It moves beyond standard diff outputs by enabling a multi-file review stream with sidebar navigation and responsive auto layouts like split or stacked views. Uniquely, it is designed for the era of AI coding, supporting inline AI and agent annotations directly alongside the code so developers can review agent-generated patches in context. It operates in real-time, utilizing watch mode to automatically reload as the working tree changes during automated refactors.
keyFeatures: Review-first interactive UI: Navigate smoothly through complex changesets with a persistent sidebar and a continuous multi-file review stream.
Inline agent annotations: View AI-generated context, explanations, and notes directly inline with code diffs for better auditing.
Responsive auto layouts: Dynamically switches between split and stacked views based on the available terminal dimensions.
Watch mode: Auto-reloads file and Git-backed reviews instantly when the working tree changes in the background.
Cross-VCS native support: Operates natively across different version control tools, including Git, Jujutsu (jj), and Sapling.
Rich input handling: Fully interactable via mouse clicks and scrolling, while also supporting a fallback pager-compatible mode.

useCases.description: Developers use Hunk to review massive patches authored by autonomous coding agents, leveraging inline annotations to understand the agent's context and decisions.

useCases.title: Interactive Local Code Review
useCases.description: Engineers reviewing their own unstaged or staged changes across multiple files using a rich terminal interface rather than scrolling through standard Git diff output.

useCases.title: Live Refactoring Validation
useCases.description: Use watch mode to continuously observe structural or wide-ranging file changes in real-time as a Python script or AST refactoring tool runs.

useCases.title: Jujutsu workflow enhancement

aiSummary.whoIsItFor: Software engineers and AI tool builders who work extensively in the terminal and need a richer way to review complex changesets, especially those generated by autonomous AI agents. Ideal for teams requiring efficient terminal UI.
